title: The Adversarial Threat Model
summary: Work through The Adversarial Threat Model.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Adversarial Threat Model** in *Agent Security* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Security, § The Adversarial Threat Model
blocks.md: In the dependency README attack, untrusted text from a third party with no authority over the repair task reaches the model through an observation channel that the task itself opened. Defending that channel begins by formalizing the interaction into an adversarial threat model that names the attacker's entry point, bounds what the payload can influence, and specifies precisely which observed side effect constitutes a security violation.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Structural prompt injection matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

questions.q: The section **The Adversarial Threat Model** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Detection only lowers the rate at which payloads get through, whereas separation by construction bounds what any payload can reach, detected or not.

Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

Human approval binds to a digest of the canonical, host-resolved action, is presented out of band with the agent's explanation labeled untrusted, and is re-verified with its preconditions immediately before dispatch.

Over a trajectory an attacker gains an adaptation oracle and conversational momentum, so every dispatch is re-evaluated against policy and an obfuscated retry after a block is still the blocked action.
